text:
Maya: Hey team, customer reporting streaming responses truncating after ~55s. They get partial output (last chunk seems cut off) and client reconnects. Happens on a Node fetch consumer behind our nginx+Cloudflare stack. Suspect proxy idle close/buffering. ticket: C-4812

Jon: Can you paste the raw response headers and a simple repro? curl -v -N to avoid buffering. Also what model / route?

Maya: Route: /v1/stream?model=gpt-pico. Customer host is behind an ALB -> nginx (proxy_pass) -> app. Headers they sent:
```
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.local
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Connection: keep-alive
```
Response headers they captured (partial):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
X-Accel-Buffering: no
```
But the client sees no more data after 55s, then eventsource reconnects.

Priya: Default ALB idle timeout is 60s. If there's no TCP-level packets for >60s it will close. But SSEs typically send heartbeats to prevent that. Does Redwood emit colon-heartbeat or newline pings?

Maya: Our runtime sends a lightweight newline every 20s: "\n" as heartbeat. Customer says they see it in server logs but not on client. Suggestion: some upstream (nginx/Cloudflare) may be coalescing or buffering tiny writes or compressing them away.

Margo: This matches a recent subtle bug: when response has gzip or http chunk coalescing enabled, some proxies buffer until a minimum chunk size or until gzip window flush. Tiny 1-byte heartbeats can be swallowed by upstream compression or NGINX proxy buffering unless we explicitly disable buffering or force flush at the app layer. Also Cloudflare edge can reassemble and apply buffering heuristics that hide micro-heartbeats.

Maya: Customer stack: ALB (TLS termination) -> Cloudflare in front? Actually they use Cloudflare spectrum + page rules, then ALB. Their nginx sits in ECS behind ALB and proxy_pass to the app at localhost:8080. They have gzip on.

Jon: Repro plan: 1) curl -v -N to the origin IP (bypass Cloudflare) 2) curl -v -N via ALB 3) curl -v -N via Cloudflare. Compare outputs and timing. Use `--raw` to preserve chunks.

Maya: I ran quick local repro against our devbox: server sends "data: x\n\n" every 20s. When nginx `proxy_buffering on` + gzip enabled, curl shows nothing until ~3rd beat, then a burst. With `X-Accel-Buffering: no` set on response it streams correctly.

Priya: Good find. For Cloudflare specifically: CF will buffer unless response is uncompressed and is marked as event-stream; they also have an internal min-chunk threshold. Workarounds: disable gzip for SSE endpoints (set `gzip off` or `gzip_proxied off`), add `Cache-Control: no-transform`, and ensure the server flushes (e.g., `res.flush()` in express) after writes. Also add a slightly larger heartbeat payload (eg 128 bytes) to cross buffering thresholds if you can't disable compression.

Margo: From runtime side we can: 1) send an explicit SSE colon ping `: ping\n\n` and flush after write, 2) ensure responses include `X-Accel-Buffering: no` by default for streaming routes, and 3) set `Content-Encoding: identity` for SSE paths to prevent gzip. But note: some customers insist on gzip elsewhere. So provide config knobs and a diagnostic header `X-Redwood-Stream-Debug: flushed/heartbeat-sent` to help triage.

Ingrid: Ops-bot created incident INC-2026 and flagged customer C-4812.

Maya: Quick mitigation provided to customer: 1) set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on their nginx location for `/v1/stream`, 2) turn off gzip for that location or set `gzip_min_length` to 1 to cheat it, 3) set ALB idle timeout to 120s if they want to avoid changing nginx. Sent script they can run:
```
# quick curl repro (bypass browser buffering)
curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.their-host.example/v1/stream' --raw
```
And a node consumer snippet:
```
fetch(url, {headers: {Accept: 'text/event-stream'}}).then(r=>{
  const reader = r.body.getReader();
  function read(){
    reader.read().then(({done, value})=>{
      if(done) return console.log('done');
      console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
      read();
    })
  }
  read();
});
```

Jon: Can engineering add a runtime flag to force non-gzip + disable buffering for streaming endpoints? Also add a short doc blurb for customers explaining proxies that buffer micro-chunks (ALB/nginx/Cloudflare) and recommended mitigations.

Margo: Yes. I'll open ENG-rt-1125 to add `streaming.force_identity_encoding` and default server header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for /v1/stream. Also adding telemetry to surface when client-heartbeats are dropped (based on time-between-server-writes).

Priya: Postmortem checklist for support: - collect full upstream chain (CF? ALB? nginx?), - get `curl -v -N` logs from each hop, - check `Content-Encoding`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `X-Accel-Buffering`, - ask customer to disable gzip for the endpoint or increase heartbeat size as quick workaround.

Maya: Customer confirmed temporary fix by setting `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and disabling gzip on nginx. We'll follow up when ENG change is deployed. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: assigned to Margo, priority P2, linked ticket C-4812

Margo: I'll keep this thread updated with the ENG ticket and rollout plan. Thanks all.
